source_text.body:
Run implementing and reviewing agents with a lead agent
A lead agent takes review findings, has an implementing agent fix them and resubmit, and pings the human only for out-of-scope decisions or repeated failed reviews.
·
Nov 18, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
A lead agent coordinates an implementing agent and a reviewing agent. When review findings come back, the lead passes the relevant ones to the implementing agent to fix and resubmit for review. The loop repeats on its own. The commenter is pinged only if a decision exceeds the lead's purview or reviews fail a set number of times.
How it went
The source gives no numbers or results. The commenter says they don't have to handle anything unless needed, and can still read what happened in the transcript afterward.
Worth knowing
Pick the failed-review limit that triggers a human ping; the source doesn't say what number is used, and it doesn't cover manual testing details.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
In my repo at [path or repo name], act as a lead agent coordinating two subagents: one that implements [feature or list of issues] and one that reviews the work. Have the reviewer report findings, send them back to the implementer to fix and resubmit, and loop until the review passes. Only stop and ask me if a finding needs a decision outside the scope of [the task], or if the same issue fails review [3] times; otherwise finish with a short summary of what changed and the final review result.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50543229
